artifacts.title: Music Kitchen product brief
artifacts.description: A personal arranging studio: play piano, write lyrics, and direct the rest of the band through musical examples.

artifacts.title: Research foundations
artifacts.description: A focused map of 27 sources, an editable musical representation, and research questions to revisit as the product develops.

artifacts.title: Studio experiment 01
artifacts.description: The first playable canvas: phrase selection, drawn contours, tapped rhythm, reversible edits, and an executable musical recipe.

artifacts.title: Earlier market positioning
artifacts.description: The earlier assessment of generation, editing, and score-based opportunities. Context for the shift toward the musician’s experience.

artifacts.title: Positioning evidence
artifacts.description: Sources, evidence grades, and assumptions behind the market assessment. Product capabilities are dated vendor claims.

entries.title: From a research agenda to a product musicians can use
entries.summary: Music Kitchen takes shape as a personal arranging studio. The key question becomes how a musician directs the second and third revision through sound, examples, and gestures.
entries.stage: Playable browser interaction prototype. Product direction and research documented; no trained music model or user study yet.
entries.focus: Select a musical phrase, draw its contour, tap a rhythm, and hear a scoped, reversible change.
entries.next_step: Try the studio with pianist-songwriters, compare correction tasks with existing tools, then investigate humming and reference transfer.
